production.note: US model years, from a database (last resort) with a publication for the first year. First: KBB lists the 2012 Aventador as 'LP 700-4 Coupe 2D' and says 'The Aventador is all-new for 2012, replacing the Murcielago'; MotorWeek road-tested the '2012 Lamborghini Aventador LP 700-4' (motorweek-aventador-2012). Last: KBB's 2017 Aventador lists 'LP 700-4 Coupe 2D' (kbb-aventador-2017), and for 2018 says 'the base model is dropped, replaced by the 740-horsepower Aventador S' with only S trims listed (kbb-aventador-2018). The Roadster is a separate record.

body.note: Two-door coupe; the open car is sold as the Aventador LP 700-4 Roadster (separate record).

aspiration.note: Naturally aspirated V12 (MPI, no forced induction listed)

drivetrain.note: '4WD with Haldex generation IV' (permanent, automatically engaging)

transmission.note: 'Gearbox: 7 speed ISR, shifting characteristic depending on drive select mode' (ISR = Independent Shifting Rods, a single-clutch automated manual); no manual offered

powerHp.note: Quote: "Maximum power: 700 HP (515 kW) at 8.250 rpm". The 700 is Lamborghini's metric (CV/PS) figure: 700 x 0.98632 = 690 hp. No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS. MotorWeek writes 'a 691-horsepower ... 6.5-liter, V12' (motorweek-aventador-2012); see discrepancies. KBB prints Lamborghini's metric figure as hp; no hp rating from Lamborghini's US arm was found, so the guide's conversion is used.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (no curb weight for the standard car, and no optioned-car curb weight, was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine). Quote: "Dry weight: 1575 Kg". 1,575 x 2.20462 = 3,472 lb. The sheet does not say whether this is with lightweight options. A car ready to drive is heavier.

sources.publisher: Autoblog.gr (Lamborghini technical data sheet reproduced in full)
sources.title: Lamborghini Aventador LP 700-4 technical data

discrepancies.reason: Conversion rounding: 700 CV (515 kW) converts to 690 hp from PS (x 0.98632) and to 691 hp from kW (x 1.34102). MotorWeek's 691 is not a separate rating.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 690 hp, the guide's PS conversion of Lamborghini's 700 CV.

discrepancies.reason: Rounding: MotorWeek writes 'a 3,500 pound dry weight', a rounded version of Lamborghini's 1,575 kg (3,472 lb) dry figure.
